* Player City — Player_City__c — Text(80)
* Player State — Player_State__c — Text(80)
* Player Country — Player_Country__c — Text(80)
* Referral Code — Referral_Code__c — Text(80) — audit only
* Rep Slug — Rep_Slug__c — Text(80) — audit only
* Sales Rep External Id — Rep_External_Id__c — Text(80) — authoritative rep id from backend
* Deal External Id — Deal_Id__c — Text(80) — raw book/can id from backend
* Related Deal — Related_Deal\__c — Lookup(Deal_\_c) — set by flow
* Book Name — Book_Name__c — Text(120)
* Type — Type__c — Text(40) — vertical as sent by backend
* Site — Site__c — Text(120)
* Book State — Book_State__c — Text(80)
* Book Country — Book_Country__c — Text(80)
* Click Timestamp — Click_Timestamp__c — Date/Time
* Survey Completed — Survey_Completed__c — Checkbox
* Related Sign Up — Related_Sign_Up\__c — Lookup(Sign_Up_\_c) — set by flow
* Processing Status — Processing_Status__c — Picklist — New (default); In Progress; Processed; Review Required; Error
* Review Reason — Review_Reason__c — Text(255)

## Implementation Requirements

* Create the custom object with the fields above; help text per design doc story E-01
* All API-sourced fields are created as optional (not required) — see open question on requiredness
* Processing Status defaults to New on insert
* List view: Clicks — Review Required

## Acceptance Criteria

* Upsert on External_Id__c is idempotent — the same backend click id never creates a duplicate
* A click with the same player/deal info but a different Click Timestamp is stored as a distinct record
* Processing Status defaults to New

## Testing Notes

Upsert the same External_Id twice; insert two clicks differing only by timestamp.

## Out of Scope

The resolution flow (POC-12 demo version, BUILD-04 production version).

## Open Questions

* Field requiredness: the design doc marks \~20 API fields required, but the current backend payload supplies only \~9 of them and several source columns are nullable. Fields are built optional until the backend field contract is agreed (call with WagerTech engineering pending). Final list to be confirmed per field: backend supplies / optional / drop.
* Type values from the backend are currently only Casino and Sports — confirm how DFS/Sweepstakes/Poker clicks will be identified before converting Type to a picklist.

## Additional Notes

* Book Country source: the backend field originally mapped for this does not hold a country — the correct source is the backend state reference table country column. Flag in the API contract.
* Sign-Up lookup field requires POC-10 to exist first — create the two objects in the same deployment or add the lookup second.

Build a record-triggered flow on Study Link Click that resolves the happy path: match or create the Player, resolve the Deal-Rep Assignment, then link or create a Sign-Up. Demo-grade only; the production flow with full review-branch handling is a separate story (BUILD-04).

## Implementation Requirements

* Record-triggered flow on Study_Link_Click__c, entry when Processing Status = New
* Player resolution: match on Player External Id, then Email; exactly one match links, zero matches creates a Player (record type Player)
* Deal-Rep Assignment resolution: match Rep External Id + Deal External Id where status = Active; exactly one match required
* Sign-Up resolution: link to an existing open Sign-Up (Status New/In Progress/Past Due/Flagged) for the same Player + Assignment, else create one with Status = New
* On success set Processing Status = Processed; on any other outcome set Review Required + a Review Reason and stop
* Name the flow with a POC prefix

## Acceptance Criteria

* Inserting a click creates/links Player and Sign-Up and sets Processed
* A repeat click for the same Player + Deal links to the existing open Sign-Up instead of creating a second one
* An unresolvable click is flagged Review Required with a reason, never errors

## Testing Notes

Three scenarios: new player, repeat click, unknown rep id.

## Out of Scope

All multi-match and error-path branch handling, async optimization (BUILD-04).

## Additional Notes

* This flow is replaced by BUILD-04; nothing else should depend on it.

---

Create Deal__c as the commercial source of truth. One Deal per Partner + Operator + Market + Vertical combination with a distinct rate; where terms differ by vertical or market, each combination is a separate Deal record.

Fields

  • Deal ID — Name — Auto Number

  • Vertical — Vertical__c — Picklist, Required — WT_Vertical global value set

  • Deal Currency — Deal_Currency__c — Picklist — CAD; USD used Currency CurrencyIsoCode instead

  • Deal Version — Deal_Version__c — Number(4,0)

  • Deal Status — Deal_Status__c — Picklist, Required — Active; Paused; Closed; Inactive; Review Required

  • CPA Target — CPA_Target__c — Number(6,0)

  • Target Period — Target_Period__c — Picklist — Monthly; Quarterly; Custom

  • CPA Value — CPA_Value__c — Currency

  • Commission Terms — Commission_Terms__c — Long Text Area(4000)

  • Priority Tier — Priority_Tier__c — Picklist — Tier 1; Tier 2; Tier 3

  • Redeposit Range Min — Redeposit_Range_Min__c — Currency

  • Redeposit Range Max — Redeposit_Range_Max__c — Currency

  • Target Average Redeposit Amount — Target_Average_Redeposit_Amount__c — Currency

  • Bonus Requirement — Bonus_Requirement__c — Number(12,2)

  • Bonus Requirement Type — Bonus_Requirement_Type__c — Picklist — CPAs; Revenue; Net Revenue; Volume; Redeposit Volume; Custom

  • Redeposit Required — Redeposit_Required__c — Checkbox, default false

  • Bonus Progress — Bonus_Progress__c — Number(12,2) — manual in Phase 1

  • Bonus Status — Bonus_Status__c — Picklist — On Track; At Risk; Behind; Achieved; Missed; Not Applicable

  • Redeposit Budget — Redeposit_Budget__c — Currency

  • Redeposit Target — Redeposit_Target__c — Number(6,0)

  • Effective Start Date — Effective_Start_Date__c — Date

  • Effective End Date — Effective_End_Date__c — Date — blank = open-ended

Implementation Requirements

  • Create the Deal__c custom object with the fields listed above; help text per design doc story C-01

  • Apply lookup filters on Partner and Operator (record-type filtered)

  • A Deal cannot be saved without Operator, Market, and Vertical (required fields)

  • Deal creatable with all required fields enforced

  • Lookup filters restrict Partner/Operator to the correct record types

Out of Scope

Duplicate-blocking on the Partner+Operator+Market+Vertical+Version key (BUILD-08). Operator-default fallback logic. Bonus progress calculation. Redeposit auto-close.

Open Questions

  • When one market covers USA and Canada, is currency a commercial differentiator (two Deals, one per currency) or one Deal with a single currency?

  • Rates in the source data change monthly — confirm a rate change means a new Deal Version, and whether rate history must be reportable in Salesforce or only in BI.

Additional Notes

  • If sprint time runs short, the bonus/redeposit fields can be created after the demo — the data load needs the first 14 fields.

## Source of truth

Living design hub:    
https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/folder/268894210

Jira-ready requirements:    
https://jumpr.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/JK/pages/269090817/03+User+Stories+Jira+Disposition

Current design baseline: **v0.12**

## Outcome

Salesforce is the master for WagerTech Deals and Affiliate Links. CMS receives every relevant post-activation state change through one supported outbound sync service; failures are visible/recoverable; Deal identity, inactivity, Link publication and safe deletion are controlled.

## Current outbound scope

* Deal lifecycle:

    * New / Activate;
    * Paused / Inactive / Closed / Review Required;
    * Reactivate;
    * Retired / successor relationship.
    
* Date-based lifecycle tracking:

    * New Date;
    * First Activated Date;
    * latest Active / Paused / Inactive / Closed / Retired / Review Required Dates;
    * Effective End Date.
    
* First Click Date on Sign-Up, Deal Last Sign-Up First Click Date rollup, formula-qualified scheduled inactivity, and Inactive auto-reactivation.
* Makeup-key reservation/release + permanent unique External Deal ID.
* Deal + Operator/Partner + Region + currency payload.
* Affiliate Links in Deal payload including stable `link_external_id`.
* generic Link `Exclude from CMS`, CMS publication markers and safe deactivate-before-delete.
* Queueable Apex sync engine.
* byte/count-aware batching, retry, stale-response protection and error handling.
* Deal sync state, manual/bulk retry, reports/alerts.
* staging verification and production cutover.
* credentials/configuration.
* Link storage hardening (WAGR-499) before production Link publication.

## Key lifecycle / identity rules

* New is the pre-activation default and is not sent.
* Deal lifecycle fields use **Date** where same-day ordering is not required.
* Automation-managed dates/markers update only on their defined source event; unrelated edits are no-op.
* First activation queues the first eligible CMS send.
* Every payload-relevant change after First Activated requests one logical sync.
* Every post-activation Deal Status change sends the Salesforce status value as-is.
* Retired, not Replaced, is terminal for normal users.
* Makeup Key and External Deal ID are separate:

    * Makeup Key reserves the business makeup.
    * External Deal ID permanently identifies a specific Deal record once activated.
    
* Only Retired releases the raw Makeup Key:
  `{raw}-R-{18-character case-safe Salesforce Deal Id}`.
* Retirement never changes External Deal ID.
* Keep existing automatic External Deal ID collision convention for replacement records: base → `-002` → `-003`…
* No user-entered Deal Version field.
* Replacement successor cannot Activate until predecessor latest Retired/successor state is confirmed Synced.
* Legacy `United States & Canada` target Market Country is deactivated; target Deal is country-wide or one state/province.

## Deal activity / inactivity

* Sign-Up First Click Date is a **Date**.
* New SLC-created Sign-Up derives it from the UTC calendar date of source `Click_Timestamp__c`.
* Repeat clicks to the same Sign-Up do not move First Click Date in V1.
* Historical import/re-parent preserves First Click Date.
* Deal Last Sign-Up First Click Date = MAX related Sign-Up First Click Date.
* Inactivity eligibility is a Formula Checkbox:

    * baseline = later applicable Date of First Activated / Last Sign-Up First Click;
    * First Activated blank fails safe;
    * exactly N days old remains Active;
    * older than N qualifies;
    * default N = 90, configurable.
    
* Scheduled Flow sweeps formula-qualified records only; it does not query Sign-Ups.
* Inactive auto-reactivation is tied only to new Sign-Up / deliberate Deal re-parent source events and requires First Click Date ≥ Inactive Date.
* Non-live activity monitoring is V1 Formula/report based; durable status-at-arrival snapshots are deferred unless historical audit is later requested.

## Integration architecture

* **Queueable Apex is the single outbound sender.**
* Normal processing is near-real-time async request → Queueable; no normal minute-based polling loop.
* Automatic/manual/bulk/full re-sync use the same service.
* Existing CDC / External Service metadata must not become a duplicate sender.
* Hard limits: ≤200 Deals and ≤1 MB; target serialized batch ceiling ≈800 KB.
* 60-second callout timeout unless contract changes.
* CMS request/attempt/success/retry and Link publication markers use **DateTime** because same-day order matters.
* No dedicated V1 per-call Integration Log; use Deal sync state + diagnostics.
* Working V1 currency mapping: CMS `currency` ← Deal `CurrencyIsoCode`; retain as explicit WagerTech confirmation.

## Affiliate Links

* Link External ID = Deal External ID + deterministic delimiter + Link Code; stored unique External ID and never silently truncated.
* WAGR-499 hardens authoritative Tracking URL storage to support the CMS 2,048-character envelope.
* Link Code maximum remains an explicit WagerTech decision; do not silently truncate.
* Multiple Link changes for one parent Deal in one transaction → one logical parent Deal sync request.
* Lightweight Link publication markers prove last confirmed CMS state.
* Previously-published Link must be current Inactive and CMS-last-confirmed Inactive before delete/exclusion can proceed.
* Protect standard UI/list/related-list/API delete paths at the backend.
* Desired CMS omission semantics (“retain last-known inactive Link state”) remain pending Strah confirmation.

## Existing compatibility questions that do not block core build

* What “Active Deal” should mean for existing Operator/Partner/OPR DLRS/count logic after new statuses are introduced.
* Final Deal currency semantics.
* Link Code maximum / migration normalization.
* Review Required setter/use case.
* Pause Reason / Link-required-at-activation / Commercial-Terms-required-at-activation.

## Later / separate workstream

**WAGR-444 — CMS → Salesforce Deal Rep Assignments.**

WAGR-49 / WAGR-50 Link attribution remains lower priority until outbound Link identity is available to CMS.

## Out of scope

* Commercial Terms in CMS payload.
* Automated Sign-Up/DRA/Link movement between predecessor/successor Deals.
* Guided clone/replace enhancement.
* CMS → Salesforce DRA implementation (WAGR-444).

## Contract note

Older source documents may refer to Replaced, user-entered Deal Versioning, authoritative Link omission/removal, or different activity semantics. The living Confluence **v0.12** design supersedes those internal assumptions where explicitly documented; external CMS contract changes still require WagerTech/Strah confirmation.

## Background

Players are Person Accounts (Player record type) created automatically by the SLC intake flows when a link click comes in from the CMS. Each Player accumulates Sign-Up records (Sign_Up\__c, linked via Playerc); a rep works a Sign-Up through Statusc = New → In Progress → Completed. Account.Player_Status_\_c tracks the player lifecycle with four values: **Pending** (default at creation), **Active**, **Inactive**, **Banned**. Today every status change is manual — in practice nothing moves, so all 100 Players in Partial sit at Pending even where sign-ups progressed.

## Outcome

Status maintains itself: first completed Sign-Up activates a Pending Player; 90 days without qualifying activity deactivates an Active one; new activity reactivates an Inactive one; Banned is set and cleared only by authorized humans via a controlled path.

## Guardrail (binds every child)

Automation only ever sets a Player to Active or Inactive, and only Players currently at **Pending, Active, or Inactive** are eligible. Banned is never set, cleared, or overwritten by automation. Audit stamping (Player_Status_Set_Date\__c + Player_Status_Last_Updated_By_\_c) is **centralized in BUILD-251**, which captures every status change regardless of source — UI edits, flows, and data loads. Individual automations do not stamp these fields themselves.

## Children & sequence

BUILD-250 and BUILD-251 are prerequisites; then BUILD-252 → BUILD-253 → BUILD-254; BUILD-255 after BUILD-251.

1. BUILD-250 — Sign-Up: Completion Date stamp (1–2 h)
2. BUILD-251 — Player: centralized status audit stamp (1–2 h)
3. BUILD-252 — Player: Last Activity Date engine, subflow (2–3 h)
4. BUILD-253 — Player: status + sign-up stamps on Completed Sign-Up (3–5 h)
5. BUILD-254 — Player: scheduled Active → Inactive at 90 days (3–4 h)
6. BUILD-255 — Player: Ban button + unban restriction (2–3 h)

Total 12–19 h. All work in **Partial SB**; prod is out of scope.

## Closure rule (every child)

Before closing, add deployed component API names to the ticket and update the requirements doc.

## UAT

Current data in Partial SB supports walking the full Pending → Active → Inactive → reactivation cycle end-to-end.

## Out of scope

* Non-Sign-Up activity sources.
* Historical-data backfill (Partial holds test data only — revisit at data migration; note the BUILD-253 flow fires on data loads that set Status = Completed, so the migration runbook must deactivate it or plan for mass activation).
* BA/Primary/Secondary Referrer defaulting on first completed Sign-Up (proposed to client, unconfirmed — separate ticket if approved).
* Notifications on deactivation.
* Prod deployment.
* Reason-based reactivation gating — today Inactive only ever means inactivity, so any Inactive Player is eligible for reactivation; revisit gating by Player_Status_Reason__c if other Inactive reasons come into use.

## Open questions

1. Qualifying activity = Completed Sign-Up only for v1 — communicated in the client Q&A doc without objection; chase explicit OK from Emily/Lina or treat the doc as sign-off.
2. BA/Referrer defaulting — awaiting client confirmation; new ticket if yes.

Signups can already name a Paused or Banned referrer without being blocked — Kobi confirmed this at the 9/24 sync, so the original "flag-don't-block" automation this ticket was built around isn't needed.

The ticket is rescoped to just surfacing a report or notification for Ops when a signup names a banned/paused referrer, since Emily noted this is a useful signal for investigating referrer networks.

Requirements

  • A report or notification surfacing signups where the named referrer's status is Paused or Banned.

Constraints

  • No changes to signup completion behavior — referrer selection and signup completion must continue working exactly as they do now (unblocked).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Ops has a way to view signups whose named referrer is currently Paused or Banned.

  2. Signup completion is unaffected — selecting a paused/banned referrer does not block or alter the signup flow.

Assumptions

  • Referrer status (Paused/Banned) is already a queryable field on the Sign-Up or Referrer record, since no new status logic is in scope here.

Open Questions

  • Reporting mechanism not yet decided — list view, dashboard component, or an alert/notification are all still on the table.

Dependencies

  • Referrer status field/model — originally tied to BUILD-185 (Referrer: Object + Core Status).

Out of Scope

  • The original flag-don't-block automation (mirrored from PL-9) — descoped, since blocking was never actually happening and no new signup-flow logic is required.

References

  • Wagertech Internal Sync, Sep 24, 2026 (~01:02:29–01:03:48)

  • Original ticket source: RF-11 — Referrer Record User Stories doc

  • Aug 18 Weekly Sync — Emily Vandenberg, "flag, don't block" (Fathom, 1:33:19)

Built the MVP for this ticket: a report that lists signups whose named referrer is Paused or Banned.

What's built

  • Report: "Sign-Ups with Paused or Banned Referrer" (standard "Sign Ups with Referrer" report type).

  • Filter: Referrer Status equals Paused or Banned.

  • Columns: Sign Up ID, Player, Referrer, Referrer Status, Created Date.

  • No automation and no change to the signup flow, so signup completion is unaffected (AC2).

Pending client decisions

  • Subscription: the report can email a snapshot to chosen users. Client to confirm who receives it, how often (daily or weekly), and whether it sends only when there are matching records (recommended).

  • Recipients must be WagerTech users who already have access to this data, and need Viewer access to the report folder.

Not yet verified

  • The report shows 0 rows today. Real data is TBD, so the Paused and Banned filter is not yet tested with live records. Testing needs a safe test referrer or a sandbox.

Notes

  • The report uses the referrer's current status, not their status at signup time. A status snapshot on the signup would be a separate build.

  • Subscription emails are scheduled, not real time. Instant alerts would be a separate build.

  • One referrer name appears with both Active and Inactive statuses across signups, which may mean duplicate referrer Accounts. Worth a data check.

Questions to ask WT:

  • Who should get the email? (WagerTech users who already have access to signup data)

  • How often: daily or weekly?

  • Should it send only when there are matching signups, or every time?

**Goal:** separate test/demo Deals from real ones so list views, reports and the CMS integration can tell them apart at a glance.

## Scope

1. New checkbox `Deal__c.Test_Deal__c` ("Test Deal"), default **false**, not required.
2. Deal `Name` gets a **-TEST suffix** when checked, and loses it when unchecked.
3. `External_Deal_ID__c` gets a **TEST- prefix** when checked — note this is a _prefix_, deliberately. See the design note below; a suffix breaks the collision handler.
4. ~~Downstream~~ `Is_Test_Deal__c` ~~formula on~~ `Sign_Up__c` ~~and~~ `Deal_Rep_Assignment__c` ~~so those objects can be filtered too.~~ Cancelling for now to keep scope tight, will add later if needed. 
5. ~~Validation rule locking~~ `Test_Deal__c` ~~after creation.~~ Cancelling for now to keep scope tight, will add later if needed. 
6. Backfill the 15 Deals loaded 2026-08-20 — all of them are test data.

## Design note — why the External Deal ID uses a PREFIX, not a suffix

The flow _Deal - Before Save - Set External Deal ID_ handles collisions by querying `External_Deal_ID__c StartsWith fxBaseKey`, sorting descending, and deriving the next number with `VALUE(RIGHT(match, LEN(match) - LEN(base) - 1)) + 1`.

With a **suffix**, a real Deal keyed `BETMGM-GD-ON-CAS` would match `BETMGM-GD-ON-CAS-TEST` on StartsWith. Descending sort puts `-TEST` above `-002` (T > 0), so the formula evaluates `VALUE("TEST")` and **the flow errors on the next real Deal**.

With a **prefix**, test Deals occupy their own `TEST-…` namespace. Real Deals never see them, test Deals collision-count among themselves. No change needed to the collision logic.

The `Name` keeps the `-TEST` suffix as requested — Name has no collision logic, so there is nothing to break.

## Formula changes

**1. Flow** _**Deal - Before Save - Set Deal Name**_**, formula resource** `DealNameFormat` — wrap the existing IF and append:

```

```

```
+ '-' + {!$Record.Operator__r.Name} + '-' + {!$Record.Partner__r.Partner_Code__c}
```

```
+ '-' + TEXT({!$Record.Vertical__c})),
```

```
UPPER({!$Record.Market_State_Code__c} + '-' + {!$Record.Operator__r.Name}
```

```

```


```
& IF({!$Record.Test_Deal__c}, '-TEST', '')
```

**2. Flow** _**Deal - Before Save - Set External Deal ID**_**, formula resource** `fxBaseKey` — prepend one line, leave the rest untouched:

```
IF({!$Record.Test_Deal__c}, "TEST-", "")
```

```
&
```

```
BLANKVALUE(SUBSTITUTE({!$Record.Operator__r.Operator_External_ID__c}, "OP-", ""), "NOOP")
```

```
& "-" &
```

```
... (existing formula unchanged from here)
```

Length is fine either way — both fields are 80 chars and the longest current value is well under 45.

## Acceptance criteria

* New Deal, box unchecked → Name and External Deal ID unchanged from today's format.
* New Deal, box checked → Name ends `-TEST`, External Deal ID starts `TEST-`.
* Two test Deals with identical operator/partner/market/vertical → second gets `TEST-…-002`.
* A real Deal created _after_ a matching test Deal still gets the clean base key, no error.
* Unticking on an existing Deal is blocked by the validation rule.
* Sign-Up and DRA list views can filter on `Is_Test_Deal__c`.
* All 15 Deals from the 2026-08-20 load are flagged and renamed.

## Backfill — the 15 existing Deals

Do NOT try to null `External_Deal_ID__c` to force regeneration — it is a required field and system validation runs before the before-save flow, so the update fails. Instead set both values explicitly in one Data Loader update: `Test_Deal__c = true` and `External_Deal_ID__c = 'TEST-' + current value`. The Name flow re-fires on save and adds the suffix on its own.

_Deploy the validation rule AFTER the backfill, or it will block it._

## Companion recommendation — not required, worth doing while we are in here

_Deal - Before Save - Set Deal Name_ is actually a **RecordAfterSave** flow despite its API name, with no entry criteria — so it issues a second DML on **every** Deal create and update. Cross-object references like `$Record.Operator__r.Name` work fine in before-save (the External Deal ID flow already does exactly that). Converting it removes a DML per save, removes the recursion risk, and makes the API name honest. Roughly 1h including regression. Raise as its own ticket if we would rather not widen this one.

Five issues found while tracing _SLC - After Save - Player, DRA and Sign Up_ end to end. None block current testing; all are real. Listed worst first.

1. **Duplicate short-circuit may never fire.** Decision `Check_if_has_Duplicate` reads `Has_Duplicates`, but the Boolean variable is declared `hasDuplicates`. `Has_Duplicates` is only an outcome name inside the `Player_Found` decision, which is not a referenceable resource. If it does not resolve, duplicate cases fall through to `Get_DRA` instead of routing to Review Required. **Verify in the org first** — this one may be a red herring if the builder resolved it differently.

1. `Get_DRA` **can run with blank inputs.** `Rep__c EqualTo ''` matches DRAs with a _null_ Rep — which is exactly what a failed rep resolution produces. A click could attach to the wrong assignment. Needs a guard.

1. **No fault connectors anywhere in the flow.** Any DML or query error surfaces as an unhandled flow fault on the SLC insert rather than a Review Required record. The CMS sees a failure it cannot interpret.

1. **Wrong variable in a lookup.** `Update_Sign_Up_with_Reason` writes `varDealRepAsignmentId` into `Related_Deal__c`; the success path writes `varDRArecord.Deal__c`. A DRA Id is landing in a Deal lookup.

1. **Ended assignments still create Sign-Ups.** `Get_DRA` does not filter on `Assignment_Status__c`, so a click against an Ended assignment produces a live Sign-Up. May be intended — worth an explicit decision either way.

CONTEXT

Person Account uniqueness for Players and Referrers is enforced by Account.Email_Record_Type_Unique__c (Text 255, unique index), stamped by the flow "Account - Before Save - Set Unique Email Address for Person Accounts" as:

RecordType.DeveloperName + ":" + LOWER(TRIM(PersonEmail))

This is what allows a Player and a Referrer to legitimately share an email address (different keys) while blocking two Players on the same address — including the async race where a batch of Study Link Clicks for the same person creates duplicate Players.

If PersonEmail is blank, no key is stamp185ed and the record sits outside the duplicate guard entirely.

The SLC flow already blocks blank emails on the integration path (Has Email decision before the email match, sets Processing Status = Review Required with reason "Blank Email Address"). This ticket closes the manual UI path.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. Saving a Player or Referrer Person Account with a blank PersonEmail is blocked, on both create and edit.

2. Operator and Partner (business) Accounts are unaffected.

3. Error displays on the PersonEmail field.

IMPLEMENTATION

Rule name: Player_Referrer_PersonEmail_Required

Formula:

AND(

OR(

RecordType.DeveloperName = "Player",

RecordType.DeveloperName = "Referrer"

),

ISBLANK(PersonEmail)

)

Error message: Email is required for Player and Referrer records.

Error location: PersonEmail field

TEST NOTES

Create Player with blank email -> blocked

Create Referrer with blank email -> blocked

Create Operator / Partner with no email -> allowed

Edit existing Player, clear email -> blocked

Reprocess an SLC with a valid email -> still completes normally

DEPLOY NOTE

Assumes zero existing Player/Referrer records with a blank PersonEmail (confirmed by Kobi 2026-08-27). Re-confirm with a count in the target org before promoting past Partial SB — if any exist, every subsequent save on those records will fail. If legacy blanks turn up, add a grandfathering clause:

OR(ISNEW(), NOT(ISBLANK(PRIORVALUE(PersonEmail))))

Validation rules also apply to Flow DML, so this doubles as a backstop if a blank ever slips past the SLC guard.

RELATED

BUILD-194 — Referrer: Dedup-on-Create (hard block)

BUILD-230 — Player: Manage Duplicate Player

BUILD-03 — Player/Referrer matching, duplicate prevention, and cross-linking

> Open and non-blocking. BUILD-272 and BUILD-273 do not depend on the answer. Raise with WagerTech when there is a natural opening.

## Decision needed

The CMS allows one deal per Operator x Partner x Region x Vertical x Source, and an Inactive deal keeps its combination because it can be reactivated. So when commercial terms change — CPA, commission, bonus requirement, redeposit terms — Salesforce cannot represent that as a second deal with the same makeup. Retire & Replace does not help: the replacement's makeup is identical, which the CMS rejects. Getting it wrong means either duplicate deals that fail to sync, or overwritten terms with no record of what a Sign-Up was actually paid under.

## Options

1. **Edit in place, rely on Field History.** No new objects. Cost: the Deal keeps no version record — partly mitigated by the stamp-don't-calculate rule, since Sign-Ups already carry their own stamped payout.
2. **Child object with effective dates** (`Deal_Terms__c`). Proper versioning; payout automation resolves the row effective on the Sign-Up date. Cost: a new object that every terms-reading automation and report must traverse.
3. **Ask WagerTech to release the makeup on Inactive.** Then Retire & Replace covers terms changes too. Cost: contradicts "the CMS never deletes a deal", and a retired deal could no longer simply be reactivated.

**Jumpr's lean:** Option 1 now; Option 2 only if WagerTech needs historical-terms reporting — the Sign-Up already stamps its own payout, so Option 2 buys less than it appears to.

## Questions for WagerTech

1. When a CPA or commission changes, do you need to see what the terms _were_ on a given date, or is the current value enough?
2. Does an Inactive deal ever come back with **different** terms, or does reactivation always mean "resume as before"?
3. Confirm Inactive does not release the combination on the CMS side — this is our working assumption, and everything above depends on it.

Summary

Two Deals with the same Operator + Partner + Market Country/State + Vertical + Source must not both exist — the CMS rejects the second with makeup_owned_by_other (409), minutes after the save, in a webhook response nobody is watching.

External_Deal_ID__c looks like it already guards this but can't: it is frozen at creation, so it describes the makeup the deal had, not the one it has.

This adds Deal_Makeup_Key__c — a text field carrying the Unique index, stamped on every save from the derivation the flow already computes — with a Custom Error that names the existing deal. Supersedes the Deal portion of BUILD-08.

Current state

  • External_Deal_ID__c is unique + external id, stamped once under an IS NULL entry filter and never rewritten. Correct for the CMS, which keys its copy of the deal on it — but useless as a live constraint.

  • Get_Highest_Match / fxNextSuffix / fxFinalId append -002/-003… when a base key collides. Never fired on a surviving record. Left in place by this ticket — see step 2.

  • No Deal duplicate rules exist. BUILD-08 has carried the block-vs-flag question since 2026-07-04.

  • Two platform constraints fix the shape: a formula field cannot be marked Unique, and a before-save flow cannot read same-record formula fields. So the guard is a stamped text field fed by a flow formula.

Proposed solution

1. New field Deal_Makeup_Key__c — Text(80)

  • Unique: YES · Treat "ABC" and "abc" as duplicates: YES · External ID: no · Required: no

  • Not added to page layouts; available to reports.

Field Description (paste as-is):

Uniqueness guard: enforces one Deal per Operator + Partner + Market Country/State + Vertical + Source, matching the CMS rule "one deal per combination"

Help Text: n/a — not on page layouts.

2. Extend the existing before-save flow — fxBaseKey already computes the derivation correctly for a before-save context, so reuse it rather than writing a third copy:

  • Remove the entry filter so the flow runs on every create and update.

  • Move the null check to a Decision before Set_External_Id: assign External_Deal_ID__c only when ISBLANK({!$Record.External_Deal_ID__c}). This keeps the id immutable once set, and makes clear-and-regenerate the one sanctioned way to change it — which BUILD-273 depends on.

  • Add an always-run assignment: $Record.Deal_Makeup_Key__c = {!fxBaseKey}.

  • Leave Get_Highest_Match, fxNextSuffix and fxFinalId exactly as they are; Set_External_Id keeps assigning fxFinalId. The suffix counter is under review and is not touched here (BUILD-276). Note what this means in practice: with the duplicate block ahead of it, the counter is unreachable — a colliding save is rejected before Set_External_Id runs — so this ticket leaves the code standing, not the behaviour. The accepted cost is a second SOQL query on every Deal save that will never return a row.

  • Relabel the flow to "Deal - Before Save - Set Deal Keys"; keep the API name

Element order: Start → Get_Existing_Makeup → Decision Duplicate_Found? → (yes) Custom Error / (no) → Decision External_Id_Blank? → (yes) Get_Highest_Match → Set_External_Id → Set_Makeup_Key.

Removing the entry filter moves the "id never changes" guarantee from a filter to a Decision branch — self-evident becomes needs-proving. AC 5 and 6 cover it; don't waive them.

3. Custom Error for the message, index for the control

  • Get_Existing_Makeup: Get Records on Deal__c where Deal_Makeup_Key__c equals {!fxBaseKey} and Id does not equal {!$Record.Id}, first record only.

  • If found → Custom Error, record-level: "A deal with this Operator, Partner, Market, Vertical and Source already exists: {existing deal Name} ({existing Deal Number}). Add a Deal Rep Assignment to that deal instead of creating a new one. If the commercial terms have changed, check with the team before creating a second deal."

4. New field Makeup_Drift__c — Formula (Checkbox), BUILD-273's completion check. Safe as a formula field: read in reports, never by the flow.

NOT(ISBLANK(External_Deal_ID__c)) && External_Deal_ID__c <> Deal_Makeup_Key__c

Field Description (paste as-is):

TRUE when a Deal's frozen External Deal ID no longer matches its current makeup — the makeup changed after the ID was stamped, or the ID predates a change to the derivation.

Help Text: n/a — not on page layouts.

5. Runbook + cross-references — fxSourceCode must mirror Source_Code__c permanently, because a before-save flow cannot read the field. Make the coupling discoverable: reciprocal notes in the field and flow descriptions (same for Market_State_Code__c / fxStateCode, Region_Code__c, and the Vertical CASE that silently falls through to XXX), plus an "Adding a new Source value" runbook section covering the Source picklist, Source_Code__c, fxSourceCode, WagerTech's CMS (which accepts only wagertech and shurzy today), and any Source-filtered list views. Custom Metadata is the graduation path if the list grows. → To be handled in a separate ticket

6. Backfill — touch-save all existing Deals so every record carries a key. Genuine legacy duplicates will reject; resolve by hand and record what was found on this ticket.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Creating or editing a Deal onto an existing makeup is blocked with a message naming the existing deal. Via Data Loader, with no flow message, it still fails on the unique index.

  2. Any one component differing — Source, Market State, Vertical — saves normally.

  3. Test Deals are separate: one colliding only with a real deal saves; two colliding test deals are blocked.

  4. An Inactive Deal keeps its key, so a retired combination is still blocked.

  5. External Deal ID never moves on save, including an edit that changes the makeup. On a legacy deal missing the Source suffix, the makeup key updates and the id does not.

  6. Clearing External Deal ID and saving restamps it from the current makeup.

  7. The suffix counter never fires. An attempt to create a second Deal on an existing makeup is blocked.

  8. Blank Source still yields NOSRC in the id.

  9. Makeup_Drift__c is TRUE on a legacy suffix-less deal and FALSE on a correctly-created one.

Out of scope

  • The -002 suffix counter — whether to remove it, replace it with a manual version selector, or keep it and relax this ticket's dedupe rule (BUILD-276). It stays untouched here.

  • Consolidating fxSourceCode / fxStateCode into formula fields (not possible in before-save) or into Custom Metadata (deferred).

Context and related tickets

Drafted 2026-09-08 from the CMS Deals Webhook guide (issued 2026-09-02) plus live verification in the Partial sandbox.

Why this exists: the CMS enforces one deal per Operator + Partner + Region + Vertical + Source and rejects a second with makeup_owned_by_other (409). Salesforce needs its own constraint so duplicates are caught at save time rather than in a webhook response minutes later.

Related:

  • BUILD-08 — Build duplicate prevention rules: Operator, Partner, Deal — supersedes its Deal scope; close once Operator/Partner rules are verified

  • BUILD-273 — Deal: Data cleanup + regenerate Deal Names and External Deal IDs — the cleanup/regeneration pass that depends on AC 6

  • DECISION-07 — Deal versioning when commercial terms change — the versioning question left open; does not block this ticket

  • BUILD-246 — Deal: Source_Code__c formula field (Source → shortcode), BUILD-247 — Deal: Include Source code in External Deal ID generation, BUILD-248 — Deal: Append Source code to Deal Name automation, BUILD-249 — Deal: Require Source on record page (Dynamic Forms) + list view column — the Source batch this builds on

Two things to know before starting:

  1. The counter has never fired on a surviving record — all 28 Deals were checked, and every counter-shaped id (TEST-000, TEST-SAMPLE-DEAL-001-099) is a hand-seeded load value. The 2026-09-01 ReBet duplicate is the one likely case it did fire; that record was deleted after manual cleanup, so it is not verifiable without the Recycle Bin. No verification step is included on this ticket for that reason.

  2. Step 5 (the Account validation rule) is a Jumpr proposal, not a client ask — cut it without affecting any acceptance criterion.

Progress field: not set at creation — it is not project-scoped on this board, so set it manually if you use it.

Correction to the pinned comment (2026-09-08)

The pinned comment above refers to a "step 5 (the Account validation rule)". That step has been removed from the description and the remaining steps renumbered — the old 6, 7 and 8 are now 5, 6 and 7. Acceptance criteria are unchanged.

Reason: BUILD-274 — Account: Auto-generate Operator and Partner External IDs generates the Operator and Partner External IDs in Salesforce, so the values feeding the Deal key are correct at the source and no downstream guard is needed. Noted under Out of scope.
On Hold until we resolve decisions in this document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KDsgXLUGtixjSIgKmW9HAGNMeoMoi1hKpBqGH4i8yBs/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.aiiwd8ktxerk

Split 2026-09-10 — counter removal moved out, ticket un-held

The External Deal ID version-suffix scope has been moved to BUILD-276 — Deal: External Deal ID version suffix — remove, replace, or keep, pending the 2026-09-11 sync. This ticket is now the dedupe key and duplicate block only, and the title changed to match.

What changed in the description:

  • Step 2 no longer deletes Get_Highest_Match, fxNextSuffix or fxFinalId. Set_External_Id keeps assigning fxFinalId, and Get_Highest_Match is back in the element order.

  • AC 7 rewritten from a removal check ("no new id contains -002") to an unreachability check — the counter is still in the flow, so the test is that the duplicate block fires ahead of it and no suffixed record is produced on any path.

  • ACs 1–6, 8 and 9 are unchanged. Both Field Descriptions and Help Text are unchanged.

  • Region_Code__c (BUILD-275) added to the step 5 cross-reference list — it is a formula field, so the before-save flow cannot read it either.

  • New out-of-scope entry pointing at BUILD-276.

Status moved On Hold → Up Next. The 2026-09-09 hold was pending the decisions doc; the part that was waiting is exactly the part that moved to BUILD-276, so nothing here is blocked.

Worth knowing before you build: keeping the counter keeps the code, not the capability. Once the makeup key ships, Get_Highest_Match can never return a row — the Custom Error fires first, and the unique index catches anything that gets past it. It is a SOQL query per save that does nothing, and a code path no test can reach. Fine as a two-week holding position; not fine permanently, which is what BUILD-276 is for.

Two flow versions instead of one. This split was merged back together on 2026-09-08 precisely because both halves touch the same flow and the split bought no rollback granularity. That is still true — the reason for re-splitting is that one half is now decision-blocked and a card cannot be half-blocked. If the sync lands on "delete the counter", the cheapest path is to fold BUILD-276 back into this ticket before either is built and close 276 unstarted.

Summary

Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c are unique keys the CMS matches accounts on, and they are also embedded verbatim in every Deal External Deal ID — but nothing in Salesforce generates them. The current 63 values were typed into a spreadsheet during the initial import, so the format holds only by hand: one OP-FORTUNE WHEELZ would put a space into a key the CMS spec says is letters and digits, and it would surface as a rejected deal rather than a bad account.

This stamps both IDs in a before-save flow on Account, when the field is blank, from the same kind of derivation the Deal ID already uses. Operator = OP- + the account Name with punctuation and spaces removed, uppercased. Partner = PT- + Partner_Code__c, normalised the same way — Partner IDs are not name-derived, so the code remains the input, and the flow normalises that field too since it is hand-entered and also feeds the Deal key. If the derivation would produce an empty key, the save is blocked with a Custom Error rather than stamping a stub.

Fixing it at the source is what lets every downstream key trust these values, so the Account validation-rule guard originally drafted on BUILD-272 is cut rather than built.

Current state

  • Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c: both Text(80), unique, case-insensitive, external id. No automation writes either — populated entirely by the import.

  • Record type spread: 58 Operator, 5 Partner, 311 Player, 7 Referrer, 9 with no record type. Every Operator has an Operator ID; every Partner has a Partner ID; the other 327 accounts have neither and must not get one.

  • The derivation reproduces all 63 existing values exactly, verified record by record. Operators follow OP- + Name with spaces and punctuation stripped, uppercased — Fortune Wheelz to OP-FORTUNEWHEELZ, No Limit Coins to OP-NOLIMITCOINS, and Bally's to OP-BALLYS, which is the one case proving apostrophes are stripped too, not just spaces.

  • Partner IDs are not derivable from the name: Catena to PT-CTM, Cipher to PT-C, GDC to PT-GD, Dietz to PT-D, Direct to PT-DIRECT. These are the Airtable partner codes, so Partner_Code__c is the only valid input.

  • Partner_Code__c is Text(40), not unique, hand-entered, and its description still frames it as a reporting convenience — it is now part of two CMS-facing keys.

  • Account.Name is already required for business accounts, so a truly blank Operator name is unreachable on every path. What is reachable is a name that normalises to empty — whitespace-only, or punctuation-only like --- — which would derive the stub OP-. That, not blankness, is the case the guard has to catch.

  • A blank Partner_Code__c is fully reachable — the field is optional, so a Partner can be created without one via UI, API or data loader.

Proposed solution

1. New flow Account_Before_Save_Set_External_Ids — before-save, create and update, no entry filter on the ID fields (the blank check is a Decision, matching the Deal pattern so a manual clear regenerates).

Gate on record type by RecordType.DeveloperName, never a hardcoded RecordTypeId — Ids differ between sandbox and production and would break the deployment.

Element order: Start → Decision Record_Type? → Operator branch / Partner branch / (neither) End.

2. Operator branch — when RecordType.DeveloperName = 'Operator':

  • Leave Name itself alone (it is the user's to control).

  • Guard: if LEN({!fxCleanName}) = 0 → Custom Error targeted at the Name field: "Operator name must contain at least one letter or number — it is used to generate the Operator External ID that the WagerTech CMS matches this account on."

  • When ISBLANK({!$Record.Operator_External_ID__c}) → assign {!fxOperatorExtId}:

"OP-" & UPPER(
SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(
TRIM({!$Record.Name}),
" ", ""), "'", ""), "’", ""), "-", ""), ".", ""),
",", ""), "&", ""), "/", ""), "(", ""), ")", "")
)

Salesforce formulas have no regex replace, so the strip is an explicit SUBSTITUTE chain. The curly apostrophe is in the list deliberately — it arrives via copy-paste and is invisible in a page layout.

3. Partner branch — when RecordType.DeveloperName = 'Partner':

  • Always assign Partner_Code__c = {!fxCleanCode} (the same chain applied to Partner_Code__c instead of Name). Normalising rather than blocking keeps data loads and updates unblocked, and the field is a code, so uppercasing it silently is safe.

  • Guard: if LEN({!fxCleanCode}) = 0 → Custom Error targeted at the Partner_Code__c field: "Partner Code is required and must contain at least one letter or number — it generates the Partner External ID and is built into every Deal ID sent to the WagerTech CMS."

  • When ISBLANK({!$Record.Partner_External_ID__c}) → assign "PT-" & {!fxCleanCode}.

3a. Why the guard lives in the flow and not in a validation rule

The guard is not a failsafe — the flow needs it to be correct. Without it a blank code stamps the stub PT-, which the unique index then owns, so the next blank-code Partner fails with a raw DUPLICATE_VALUE pointing at a record that has nothing to do with it. One malformed save poisons every later one.

That inverts the usual ordering: the flow is the primary control and a validation rule would be the redundant copy. Before-save flows run before validation rules, both cover every path (UI, API, data loader, Apex), and a Custom Error can target a specific field so it renders inline exactly like a validation rule would. Building both means the same rule in two places that can drift. Decided: flow only, no validation rule.

3b. Make Partner Code mandatory in the UI — part of this ticket

The flow is the hard control; this is the prompt that keeps users from meeting it. Follow the BUILD-249 pattern rather than field-level required:

  • Mark the Partner_Code__c component required in Dynamic Forms on the Partner record page. Not field-level required, no validation rule — UI creation demands it while API, flow and data-load paths stay open (the flow guard covers those).

  • Verify the New Partner path honours it. If that modal still renders the classic layout, mark the field required there too.

  • Place it near Partner Name / Partner Type, not buried in a later section.

Raise with WagerTech before or alongside the build. Partner Code is NOT in Emily's mandatory-field list on BUILD-269 (Name, Logo, Partner Portal, Primary Contact) — this is a Jumpr addition driven by the External ID depending on it. Tell her that, rather than letting a rep discover a new required field. There are only 5 Partners and all already have codes, so nothing existing is blocked.

Convention note: layout-required is a deliberate exception to the Aug 17 rule that nothing is marked required on layouts — the same exception already granted for Source on Deal (BUILD-249), and for the same reason: a validation rule would also block updates to legacy records.

4. Duplicate handling — loud, no counter. Both ID fields are already unique, so two accounts normalising to the same value fail on the index. Add a Custom Error naming the existing account so the message is actionable:

"An account with this External ID already exists: {existing account Name}. External IDs are generated from the account name (Operator) or Partner Code (Partner), so two records cannot share one. Check whether this account is a duplicate, or adjust the name/code."

No -002 counter, deliberately: the CMS maps accounts by external id, so a counter-suffixed account would be a second identity for the same real-world operator.

5. Partner_Code__c description — replace the current text:

Field Description (paste as-is): Short uppercase code identifying this partner (e.g. CTM for Catena, GD for GDC). Set by the user, then normalised on save by flow Account - Before Save - Set External Ids: spaces and punctuation removed, forced uppercase. This value is embedded in Partner_External_ID__c AND in every Deal External Deal ID sent to the WagerTech CMS, so changing it on an existing partner does not retro-update those keys — treat it as fixed once deals exist against the partner.

Help Text (paste as-is): Short uppercase code for this partner, letters and digits only (e.g. CTM, GD). Used in the Partner External ID and in Deal IDs sent to the CMS — set it once and leave it.

6. No backfill. All 63 existing IDs already match what the flow would generate, so there is nothing to correct. Verify by spot-checking rather than by rewriting: no existing ID should change value when its account is re-saved. All 5 Partners already have codes, so the new guard blocks nothing that exists today.

Acceptance criteria

  1. A new Operator saved with a blank ID gets OP- + its uppercased, stripped name. Verify with a multi-word name and one containing an apostrophe.

  2. A new Partner with a Partner Code gets PT- + the cleaned code.

  3. Partner Code is normalised on every save — {{ctm }} becomes CTM — while the Partner External ID stays frozen.

  4. Empty derivations are blocked, not stamped. A Partner saved with a blank or punctuation-only Partner Code is blocked with the error on that field; an Operator whose name normalises to nothing is blocked with the error on Name. In neither case is a stub PT- or OP- written.

  5. The blank-code block holds on every path — UI, API and data loader — and no PT- value exists in the org afterwards to poison later saves.

  6. Existing IDs never change. Re-saving all 58 Operators and 5 Partners, including after a rename, leaves every Operator_External_ID__c and Partner_External_ID__c byte-identical.

  7. Clearing an ID and saving regenerates it from the current name or code.

  8. Player, Referrer and no-record-type accounts are untouched — no ID stamped, no Partner Code written.

  9. A second account normalising to an existing ID is blocked with the Custom Error naming the existing account; no -002 value is ever produced.

  10. The flow references RecordType.DeveloperName, not a hardcoded RecordTypeId, and deploys to a second org without edits.

  11. Partner Code is required in the UI — a new Partner cannot be saved from the record page or the New modal without it, while API, flow and data-load paths remain open.

  12. No validation rule is created on Account.

Out of scope

  • Retro-updating IDs after a rename, and any drift flag for it — the CMS matches accounts on the stored ID and does not re-derive it, so a rename is harmless.

  • Getting WagerTech to map a newly created account on the CMS side; until they do, deals on it are rejected as unknown_operator / unknown_partner. Operational, not a build step.

  • Making Partner_Code__c unique — worth considering separately, but it would need a duplicate cleanup first.

  • Partner-name duplicate rules — those stay in BUILD-08.

Output

One flow deployed in Partial SB, metadata retrieved and committed; Partner_Code__c description, help text and Dynamic-Forms-required setting applied; the Partner Code requirement raised with WagerTech; spot-check results recorded on this ticket.
